The gate is genuinely met: both independent v3 verdicts are ACCEPT at 0 blockers / 0 SHOULD-FIX / 0 advisories, and the Claude 2 verdict independently names DR-110 as its register row.

The row token is right for this specific row — plain OPEN, not the 'OPEN / inherits hard blockers' token carried by DR-106 / DR-109 / DR-113. This is the precise distinction the attack list flags, and the draft gets it correct.

The candidate/grant firewall is stated four separate ways (item 2 twice, item 4 twice) and is corroborated by D-002's recorded DR-110 deferral: 'install is fresh signed download in slice 1'. The draft's 'owner disposition remains unrecorded' is accurate — D-002 states the DR-110 disposition, 'when authored', must still draw the DR-107/G18 boundary, and no such disposition exists in COORD.

The draft anticipates its own custody drift and supplies the re-measure mechanism, which is what makes the two adoptions that landed mid-review absorbable without a retarget.

verdictRule: CONSENT only when MUST-FIX = 0 and SHOULD-FIX = 0, with custody valid or the dispatch's PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT exception applicable and verified.
verdictRationale: Seventeen refutation attempts were run, covering every item on the dispatch's attack list plus five additional angles of my own (double-recording, 'successor' overstatement, adopted-set truth, non-SATISFY list completeness, and reversibility-token collision). None produced a MUST-FIX or a SHOULD-FIX. The draft's five pinned digests all re-measure MATCH; the dual-ACCEPT 0/0 gate is genuinely met; DR-110's OPEN token is stated correctly and specifically for this row; and the candidate/grant/implementation firewalls are explicit and corroborated by D-002. The two defects I did find are an ordinal in a non-binding disambiguation aside that aged after the freeze (ADV-D121-C2-01, raised on its own merits and not shielded by any exception) and stale references to D-118/D-120 caused solely by verified append-only COORD growth (ADV-D121-C2-02). Neither bears on what D-121 records, grants, or satisfies, so neither meets the SHOULD-FIX bar. CONSENT.
